verdict: Ready with fixes, pending browser acceptance

findings.title: Idle commands ignore lease loss
findings.why_it_matters: A compact or settings command could mutate the Pi session after another worker had recovered its expired lease, creating duplicate or out-of-order session state.
evidence: Idle commands previously had no cancellation monitor while prompt turns did.
runIdleCommand now aborts the Pi session on cancellation and checks the lease before execution and completion.
packages/worker/src/processor.test.ts covers lease loss during a compact command.
findings.resolution: Added lease-aware cancellation, Pi abort, and pre/post execution guards.

findings.title: Prompt idempotency creation is non-atomic
findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent retries with one idempotency key could create duplicate user messages and jobs before the command uniqueness constraint resolved the race.
evidence: The idempotency lookup now occurs inside the same immediate transaction as all prompt-side inserts.
The transaction returns the original message, job, transcript sequence, and command when the key already exists.
packages/db/src/repositories-core.test.ts verifies a duplicate key creates no extra transcript state.
findings.resolution: Moved lookup and creation into one immediate transaction and added a regression test.

findings.title: Runtime cache aliases legacy sessions
findings.why_it_matters: Migrated sessions sharing generation 1 could receive a runtime configured for another provider, base URL, or model.
evidence: Migration 043 assigns generation 1 to all existing provider sessions.
runtimeCacheKey now includes generation, provider name, base URL, and model.
packages/agent/src/model-runtime-manager.test.ts verifies two legacy model bindings receive distinct runtimes.
findings.resolution: Expanded runtime cache identity and added legacy-session isolation coverage.

advisory_outputs.note: Back up SQLite, Pi JSONL, configuration, and state together before migration 043; rollback requires the matching set.

Monitor stale leases, interrupted jobs, projection identity conflicts and lag, command/job status counts, provider generations, null projection cursors, actor count, queue age, and approval continuation failures.
Browser acceptance remains pending until headed or headless mode is selected.
